#### 1. choroidal dystrophy, central areolar, 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.799)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2514859)

**Proposed mechanism:** GUCY2D (HGNC:4689) —DISRUPTS→ Retinal guanylate cyclase activity (GO:0000166); Retinal guanylate cyclase activity (GO:0000166) —DECREASES→ cGMP levels in photoreceptor cells (CHEBI:17041); cGMP levels in photoreceptor cells (CHEBI:17041) —DISRUPTS→ Photoreceptor cell function and survival (GO:0048749); Photoreceptor cell function and survival (GO:0048749) —LEADS_TO→ Leber congenital amaurosis (HP:0000564); Photoreceptor cell function and survival (GO:0048749) —LEADS_TO→ Central areolar choroidal dystrophy (HP:0011682). Loss-of-function mutations in GUCY2D disrupt retinal guanylate cyclase activity, leading to decreased cGMP levels in photoreceptor cells. This impairment disrupts photoreceptor cell function and survival, ultimately causing Leber congenital amaurosis and central areolar choroidal dystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in GUCY2D that lead to a gain-of-function mechanism in either disease, or the discovery of distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on cGMP signaling or photoreceptor function. _(variant: rs751761132)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving GUCY2D and cGMP signaling in both LCA1 and central areolar choroidal dystrophy could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring or modulating cGMP levels to treat both conditions.
